issue.title: ledger-tools FakeNode suites OOM instead of reporting when a strict assert comparing two nodes fails
issue.description:
Proposed by epic phase bead bob-cli-c5.3 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP), triaged by the bob-cli-c5 land agent.

Every bob-plugins ledger-tools DOM suite defines its own `FakeNode` (`parentNode`, `children`, `ownerDocument`, `inserted`/`removed` arrays, listener maps), so any node graph is cyclic. When an `assert.equal` / `assert.deepEqual` from `node:assert/strict` that compares two live FakeNodes FAILS, Node builds the AssertionError diff from the whole reachable graph and never finishes: the process grows to the heap limit and aborts with `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit ... JavaScript heap out of memory` instead of printing the failure.

Independent reproduction (land agent, 2026-10-25): copy `class FakeNode` from `scripts/test-ledger-tools-day-strip-plan-host.cjs` into a scratch file, build an 85-node tree (depth 3, fan-out 4, one click listener per node), then run `assert.equal(root.children[0], root.children[1])` under `node --max-old-space-size=1024`: it aborts with a heap OOM after ~10 s (exit 134). The same assert on a 6-node tree reports normally in ~50 ms, so the trap only springs once a test holds a realistically painted tree (a plan block plus Day strip).

c5.3 hit it as a ~33 s hang then a 4 GB abort and worked around it in the plan-host suite with boolean identity asserts (`assert.ok(planChildren(el)[1] === container, ...)`), but any future failing node-identity or node-deepEqual assert in these suites will OOM instead of reporting.

Likely fix: give each FakeNode a short `[require("node:util").inspect.custom]()` descriptor (tag, class, child count) or move the suites onto one shared FakeNode helper that has it, then convert the workaround `assert.ok(a === b)` identity checks back to `assert.equal` so failures name both nodes.

task_type_fields.impact: Any future failing FakeNode identity/deepEqual assert in the ledger-tools DOM suites (day-strip, plan-host, hosts, stats-block, stats-panels, stats-charts, reading-board) aborts the run with a heap OOM after a long hang, hiding which assertion failed.
